_comment: Cross-language parity fixture for the canonical Diagrams class-prefix sanitiser — consumed by tests/test_diagrams_class_name_parity.py (Python) AND launcher/src-tauri/tests/diagrams_class_name_parity.rs (Rust). Each [input, expected_prefix] entry pins the behaviour of vco_lib.project_init.sanitize_for_weaviate_class (Python source-of-truth) AND launcher/src-tauri/vct-hub/src/config_api.rs::sanitize_diagrams_class_prefix (Rust mirror) AND claude_mcp_servers/weaviate_mcp/server.py::_sanitize_collection_prefix (Python MCP — delegates to vco_lib.project_init). Drift between ANY of the three layers fails this fixture's parity tests. The bug being pinned (cr-b2, 2026-05-25): the Rust + MCP layers used a divergent underscore-replace algorithm for non-alphanumeric inputs, silently breaking cross-project diagrams visibility. See knowledge/concepts/cross-language-sanitiser-divergence-cr-b2.md for the post-mortem.
_comment_cases: All entries above MUST produce the listed output across all three layers. Note that this rule is INTENTIONALLY DIFFERENT from canonical_class_prefix (project_naming.json) — that one preserves underscores ('Camel_Case' stays 'Camel_Case'), this one drops them ('Camel_Case' → 'CamelCase'). The two rules coexist by historical accident: canonical_class_prefix is used for code-graph collections (CodeFunction/CodeClass/etc.) where the on-disk schema convention keeps underscores; sanitize_for_weaviate_class is used for KG/Dev/Diagrams collections where it doesn't. See knowledge/concepts/canonical-class-prefix-design.md for the history of the two-sanitiser split.
_comment_fallback: Inputs that fall back to 'vct' (lowercase, intentional — Weaviate uppercases first char on POST regardless, and the prefix flags the class as installer-managed). Triggered when nothing survives the split-on-non-alphanumeric pass, OR when the surviving PascalCase result starts with a non-letter (leading-digit case '12_project' / '123abc' / '9' — '12' and '123' are kept as digits but the leading digit is invalid for a Weaviate class).
_comment_unicode: Non-ASCII chars are treated as separators (regex [^A-Za-z0-9]+), so 'étude' loses the 'é' and produces 'Tude' (matches the existing install.py / _derive_project_kg_name behaviour exactly). '_only_' splits to ['only'] → 'Only' (no fallback — there's a valid surviving part). Unicode-aware sanitisation is out of scope — would require a migration plan for any project that already exists with a stripped name.
